payload.headline: Meta drops 3.27% to 596.22, breaks support; still wait for January earnings

summary.thesis: Sales are still growing fast at 27.53%, but heavy spending has cut free cash flow from 44.8B to 28.6B, and today's 596.22 still prices in a recovery that has not shown up yet.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait. Swing: wait. The price is falling into support in a downtrend, and the deciding event is the 2027-01-27 report.
summary.act_at: Buy at 475.85; reassess at the 576.61 support; trim near 707.21

payload.happening: Meta fell 3.27% to 596.22. It closed below yesterday's support at 605.33 and is now in the 591.53–598.97 zone, below its 20-day average (622.65, falling), its 200-day average (628.43) and its 50-day average (678.33). The Financial Times reported that Meta paused its plan for a non-voting share class after an investor lawsuit. This is preliminary and not confirmed by a filing. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: What changes the business: demand is still strong but slowing. Sales grew 27.53% over the last twelve months, but quarterly growth fell from 33.08% two quarters ago to 26.07%. Margins are where the damage is. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) fell from 43.23% to 32.86%. Free cash flow (cash left after running the business and paying for investment) fell from 44.8B to 28.6B, which leaves a free cash flow margin of only 11.86%. The balance sheet has moved from cash-rich to roughly neutral: 11.2B in cash against 83.7B in debt, for net cash of -1.2B. Liquidity of 82.4B means there is no funding stress. The filings flag that profit per share is lagging sales and that the last quarter missed forecasts by 29%. What changes only sentiment or governance: the reported pause of the non-voting share class affects shareholder rights, not revenue. Reported creator skepticism about Instagram's affiliate program, a speculative $300 price for Muse Charm, and 3D movies on Quest are small side products with no visible effect on the numbers. At risk: margins and cash flow, if the spending does not pay off. Not at risk: the core ad business's gross margin of 81.03% and its sales growth.

worth.text: The two valuation methods disagree because they start from different numbers. The cash-flow model (DCF, which values a company by its future cash) starts from today's depressed 28.6B in free cash flow. Its values are 240.54 (bear), 367.61 (base) and 498.7 (bull), all below the price. Even 30% starting growth only gives 463.29. At yesterday's 616.38, the price implied 36.9% starting cash-flow growth, which is above every growth input in DATA. The price-to-sales method (comparing the price to Meta's own past ratio of price to sales) gives 475.85 (low), 707.21 (mid) and 881.21 (high). Because it starts from sales, it assumes margins return to normal. Meta trades at 6.3 times sales. The peer median is 6.2, the growth-adjusted ratio versus peers is 1.01, and the current ratio sits at the 38th percentile of Meta's own 5-year history. The trailing P/E (price divided by the last year's profit per share) is 20.4. On a sales basis the stock is fairly priced. On a cash basis it is expensive. If operating margin fell to 24%, the cash-flow value would drop to 237.86. My range runs from the low end of Meta's own history to its midpoint.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers toward the earlier 44.8B as the spending pays off, instead of staying near 28.6B.

bull: Sales are still growing 27.53% a year on a 241.6B base, with 6.25% growth from last quarter to this one.
Gross margin of 81.03% shows the core product is still very profitable before the heavy spending on R&D (31.68% of sales).
At 6.3 times sales, Meta is priced in line with the peer median of 6.2 and sits at only the 38th percentile of its own 5-year range.
bear: Free cash flow fell from 44.8B to 28.6B, and every DCF value, including the 498.7 bull case, is below 596.22.
Operating margin dropped from 43.23% to 32.86%, and the last quarter missed forecasts by 29%.
The price is in a downtrend, below the 20-day (622.65), 50-day (678.33) and 200-day (628.43) averages, and the committee call is Reduce.

levels.what: Bottom of the next support zone (576.61–586.24, 3 touches). A close below it opens the 553.09–558.63 zone and signals the downtrend is continuing.
Low end of Meta's own price-to-sales history and close to the 463.29 DCF value at 30% growth. Buying here does not depend on a full margin recovery.
Midpoint of Meta's own history. Above it, the price treats the cash-flow recovery as already done, so trimming would be the action there.

longterm.why: 596.22 is still above every DCF value, the business is graded C, and cash flow is falling. Buying now means paying in advance for a margin recovery that the January report has not confirmed.

swing.why: The trend is down, the technical read is negative, and the nearest resistance at 605.33 is less than one average daily move (ATR 22.17) away, which leaves too little room to a target. Enter only if the price holds 576.61–586.24 or closes back above 611.95.

decision.timing: Options price a 9.4% move by Dec 18 and a 17.1% move by Feb 19, which includes the 2027-01-27 report. That report is the deciding event, so there is no long-term entry before it unless the price reaches 475.85 first.

change_mind: A close above 632.87 (the top of the 7-touch resistance zone, above the 20-day average of 622.65) would end the lower-highs pattern and allow a swing entry.
If the 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin moving back toward 43.23% and free cash flow rising from 28.6B toward 44.8B, the long-term stance moves to buy at support.
A close below 553.09 (the bottom of the lower support zone) would move the long-term stance from wait to avoid until the report.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: the decision is still wait. The close below the 605.33 support into the 591.53–598.97 zone confirmed the weakness yesterday's note flagged.
